ai_impact.ai_revenue_disclosed: AI revenue NOT separately disclosed. Management stated qualitatively (release, CFO outlook) that 'our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization' — no AI revenue figure is given, so AI ROI cannot be calculated reliably and is NOT estimated here.
ai_capex_commentary_as_disclosed: Q3 2026 capital expenditures incl. finance-lease principal were $34.91B (release); FY2026 capex guidance raised at the low end / narrowed to $135-145B from $130-145B (release). Capex is not split into AI vs non-AI by the company in the release — no AI-only capex figure is asserted.

CFO outlook (release): 'we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives'; current and scheduled capacity gives flexibility across 'model training, core business growth, and the development and support of new products'.

CFO outlook (release): MSL (Meta Superintelligence Labs) investments 'will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business' — management's own timeline caveat, paraphrased from the release.

CEO statement in release (verified quotation): 'We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model' and 'Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we're seeing velocity across the board.'

10-Q MD&A: R&D expense growth driven in part by higher data-centre / technical-infrastructure expense and 'third-party AI token costs' (paraphrase of filing text). Q3 R&D was $20,054M, +32% YoY (release income statement, calculated YoY).

other_material_items: Board approved a new non-voting Class C common stock (effective Jan 19, 2027) with a one-share Class C stock dividend per Class A/B share, expected to be economically similar to a 2-for-1 split in Class A price terms per the release; purpose stated as financing growth incl. AI infrastructure, employee compensation and potential acquisitions (release).

earnings_quality.rationale: Revenue +26% reported and constant-currency with ad price +14% and impressions +10% is genuine operating growth; ex-charge operating income $22.88B (+11.4% YoY, calculated). But GAAP operating income fell 37% on the $9.89B legal charge, total costs rose 68% YoY, and SBC was $7.36B in the quarter.

forward_outlook.rationale: Q4 2026 revenue guide $73-76B (midpoint above the labelled pre-release street figure ~$73.56B); FY capex low end raised; Reality Labs losses guided down in 2026 ($18-19B) and to ~$15B in 2027; management qualitatively guided to sustained strong revenue growth through 2027 (no FY2027 number provided). Partially offset: FY expense outlook raised to $175-179B (to incorporate the legal charge) and further youth-related litigation is flagged by management itself.

cash_quality.verdict: Weak in the quarter (Mixed on TTM)
cash_quality.rationale: OCF was strong at $32.79B, but capex of $34.91B incl. leases exceeded it: company-defined FCF -$2.12B, standard FCF -$1.16B, FCF conversion negative. On a TTM basis FCF is still positive (standard +$28.65B; company-defined +$25.13B, both calculated), so the weakness is investment-driven and current-quarter, not a collapse in cash generation. No buybacks in Q3 to offset $7.36B of SBC.
